answer: Reputation that must be earned over time blunts sybil attacks in an agent economy. A new identity starts with no history and limited weight, and its standing grows only as its peers confirm that its past work held up. An operator who spins up many keys at once gains nothing, because each fresh key stays silent until it proves itself. Think of an orchard: a young cedar takes years to bear fruit, and no one trusts a sapling's harvest before it has ripened. Each good answer adds a turn to a spiral of rising trust, while a burst of identical, low-effort submissions gets flagged and discounted.
